1	# Watch movement: going train and hands, a 6-hour variant and an assembly plan
2

4	times the size of a 25.6 mm (11 1/2-ligne class) movement, to be made by 3D printing or a similar process; that
5	process is why its smallest feature is 0.2 mm.
6	
7	## The goal
8	
9	The wearer reads the time from four hands: hours and minutes on a common centre, seconds, and a 24-hour hand that
10	shows the hour of the day. The movement takes its power from the barrel named in the order, fits the case named
11	in the order, and its parts can be printed by the process the order names. The same calibre is also built for a
12	faster running of the same barrel, on the same frame. The workshop assembles the 8-hour build part by part,
13	following your assembly plan.
14

16	and no winding or setting works: the barrel is the driver and turns at the steady speed given in the order.

18	## Order
19	
20	| Item | Specification |
21	|---|---|
22	| Barrel | part no. BR-096-20, catalogue sheet DS-W01; supplied as `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/supplied/barrel.stl` |
23	| Case | part no. CS-414-134, catalogue sheet DS-W02 |
24	| Parts | printed by the process of sheet DS-W03 |
25	| 8-hour build (`movement.json`) | barrel BR-096-20 turning clockwise, seen from the dial side, once every 8 h |
26	| 6-hour variant (`variant_6h.json`) | the same barrel BR-096-20, in the same place, turning clockwise, seen from the dial side, once every 6 h |
27	
28	## Deliverables
29	
30	Everything goes into the folder `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/`:
31	
32	| Path | Content |
33	|---|---|
34	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/movement.json` | the 8-hour build, with hour, minute, seconds and 24-hour hands |
35	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/variant_6h.json` | the 6-hour variant: the same calibre on the same frame, with hour, minute, seconds and 24-hour hands |
36	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/assembly.json` | the order in which the parts of `movement.json` are put in, and the path of each |
37	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/parts/<name>.step` | every part of both movements, one STEP file per part; a part used in both movements is one file |
38	| `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/scripts/` | optional: the scripts that made the parts. Archived with the delivery; never run or read |
39	
40	The file formats, the size limits and the JSON layouts are in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md`.
41	
42	Installed software: Python 3 with CadQuery 2.8.0 (OpenCASCADE, importable as `cadquery` and `OCP`), `manifold3d`,
43	`trimesh`, `numpy` and `scipy`; and two programs in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/tools/`:
44	
45	- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/tools/kernel.py`: a Python module of geometry helpers on `manifold3d`: read and write binary STL, rigid
46	  transforms, intersection volume, smallest distance, cross-sections, `write_step(path, shape)` (a CadQuery object
47	  or an OCP shape, written in millimetres), and `load_step_part(...)`, which turns a STEP file into the solid that
48	  the inspection measures when it is called with the numbers in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md`.
49	- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/tools/check_format.py`: `python3 /tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/tools/check_format.py` checks the file format of `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/`
50	  against `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md` (the JSON layouts, the names, and every part file read and turned into a solid as the
51	  inspection does) and prints `format ok`, or each format error it finds. It runs none of the checks of the

54	## Supplied
55	
56	- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/datasheets/`: the barrel catalogue (DS-W01), the case catalogue (DS-W02) and the print service's
57	  process sheet (DS-W03); `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/datasheets/INDEX.md` lists them.
58	- `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/supplied/barrel.stl`: barrel BR-096-20 as a mesh, in its assembled position (DS-W01, section 3). It is not

61	## Acceptance test
62	
63	The delivery is inspected after you hand it in. What is in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/` when you finish is what is inspected.
64	
65	The inspection has four parts. Each part is judged on its own, even when another part fails. Within Parts 1 to 3
66	each check counts on its own; in Part 4 each installed part counts. The delivery as a whole is accepted only when
67	every condition and every check of all four parts passes: everything must work.
68	
69	Terms used below:
70	
71	- **Frame and units.** Millimetres (mm), cubic millimetres (mm3) and degrees. A right-handed frame. Every arbor
72	  (rotation axis) is parallel to z. The dial side is +z: the hands are read looking from +z towards -z, and
73	  "clockwise" always means clockwise in that view.
74	- **Solids.** Every test measures the solids built from the part files as `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md` describes; the barrel
75	  is the solid of `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/supplied/barrel.stl`. "Intersect by at most 0.01 mm3" means that the volume of the
76	  intersection of the two solids is at most 0.01 mm3.
77	- **The frame** is the fixed parts of a movement, taken together.
78	- **A mobile** is a set of parts that turn together as one rigid body about the vertical line through its axis.
79	  The barrel is the mobile `barrel`, with its axis on x = 0 mm, y = 0 mm.
80	- **Speeds** are worked out from the tooth counts declared under `meshes`, as exact fractions, starting from the
81	  barrel at the speed the order gives for the build being judged. Every declared mesh is external: its two
82	  mobiles turn in opposite directions.
83	- **Computing time.** Each condition and each check has up to 600 s of elapsed (wall-clock) time on the
84	  inspection machine, and the whole inspection has up to 3600 s; a condition or check that runs out of time, or
85	  that would start after the whole inspection's time has run out, fails.
86	
87	### Part 1: going train and hands (`movement.json`)
88	
89	The 8-hour build: the barrel turns clockwise once every 8 h.
90	
91	Conditions. If one fails, Part 1 fails and none of its checks passes.
92	
93	- **C1 Files.** `movement.json` and every part file it names are valid as `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md` describes. A hand
94	  entry that is present and does not name a mobile of the file and one of that mobile's parts makes the file not
95	  valid; `hour`, `minute` and `seconds` must be present.
96	- **C2 Assembled.** In the assembled positions: taking the frame as one solid and each mobile (the barrel included)
97	  as one solid, no two of these solids intersect by more than 0.01 mm3; no two fixed parts intersect each
98	  other by more than 0.01 mm3; no two parts of one mobile intersect each other by more than 0.01 mm3. The fixed
99	  parts form one frame: two fixed parts are joined when their smallest distance is at most 0.01 mm, and every
100	  fixed part is joined to every other through a chain of joined fixed parts.
101	
102	Checks. Each passes or fails.
103	
104	1. **Free to turn.** Each mobile, the barrel included, turned through one full turn about its axis in 72 steps of
105	   5 degrees, never intersects the frame by more than 0.01 mm3.
106	2. **Held.** Each mobile, the barrel included, is moved 0.3 mm along +x, -x, +y, -y, +z and -z in turn, and is
107	   held in every one of the six directions. Only the tested mobile moves; the frame and every other mobile stay
108	   where they are. Moved in a direction, a mobile is held when it intersects the frame by more than 0.01 mm3, or
109	   intersects by more than 0.01 mm3 a mobile whose axis is within 0.01 mm of its own and which is itself held
110	   in that direction; this is worked out until nothing changes. A mobile whose axis is further than 0.01 mm
111	   from its own never holds it.
112	3. **Seated.** Every part of a mobile that has more than one part, moved 0.3 mm along +x, -x, +y and -y in turn,
113	   intersects the other parts of its mobile by more than 0.01 mm3 every time, and moved 0.3 mm along +z or along -z
114	   (at least one of the two) intersects them by more than 0.01 mm3. The parts of each such mobile form one piece:
115	   every part is linked to every other by a chain of parts of that mobile, each within 0.02 mm of the next.
116	   The barrel and mobiles of one part are not tested.
117	4. **The train runs.** At least one mesh is declared; no mobile is given two different speeds by the declared
118	   meshes; every declared mesh passes the mesh test below; and every mobile is driven from the barrel through
119	   declared meshes that pass the mesh test.
120	
121	   *Mesh test.* For a declared mesh, D is the mobile that the declaration names as `driver` (z_D teeth, its
122	   `driver_teeth`) and N the mobile it names as `driven` (z_N teeth, its `driven_teeth`), whichever way the power
123	   flows in the movement. D and N are whole mobiles: every part of each (for `barrel`, the supplied barrel).
124	   Starting from the assembled positions, at step i (i = 0, 1, ..., 8 x max(z_D, z_N) - 1) D is turned
125	   counter-clockwise by i x 360 / (8 x z_D) degrees about its axis, and N clockwise by that angle x z_D / z_N
126	   about its own axis. These turning senses are a convention of the test; they do not depend on the running sense
127	   of the barrel. Three conditions must hold:
128	   - no jam: at every step, and at two more positions after every 8th step (i + 1/3 and i + 1/5 in the formula
129	     above, for i = 0, 8, 16, ...), D and N intersect by at most 0.01 mm3;
130	   - engaged: at every 4th step (i = 0, 4, 8, ...) at which their intersection is empty, their smallest
131	     distance is at most 0.1 mm;
132	   - the teeth drive: at every 8th step (i = 0, 8, 16, ...), D is turned a further 0.25 of its tooth pitch
133	     (90 / z_D degrees, counter-clockwise) while N stays where it is. V is the volume of the region that the
134	     turned D shares with N and that D did not occupy before this extra turn; H is the height in z of that region;
135	     m = 2 x (distance between the two axes in the assembled positions) / (z_D + z_N) is the mesh's module. V is
136	     at least 0.001 mm3 and V / H is more than 0.5 x m x m, at every one of these steps. (V / H is the area that
137	     the extra turn cuts into N's teeth.)
138	5. **The train runs with its arbors slightly out of place.** Every declared mesh also passes the mesh test with
139	   the driven mobile N moved 0.03 mm straight away from D's axis, and with N moved 0.03 mm straight towards
140	   D's axis (N then turns about its moved axis; if the two axes coincide, "away" is +x and "towards" is -x). The
141	   steps, the turning angles and m are those of the assembled positions. This check does not change which meshes
142	   drive the hands; that is decided in the assembled positions only.
143	6. **Nothing else collides.** Every pair of mobiles (the barrel included) that is not declared as a mesh is turned
144	   together, each at its speed from the declared tooth counts (a mobile that no declared mesh reaches from the
145	   barrel stands still): 144 equal steps covering one full turn of the faster of the two, then, if their speeds
146	   differ, 144 equal steps covering one full turn of one relative to the other. At every step they intersect by
147	   at most 0.01 mm3.
148	7. **Hour hand.** 8. **Minute hand.** 9. **Seconds hand.** The hands show the time: each of the three moves as
149	   that hand of a watch does. A hand is driven only through declared meshes that pass the mesh test (a declared
150	   mesh that fails it drives nothing), and no mobile may be given two different speeds by the declared meshes.
151	10. **Hours and minutes on a common centre.** The axes of the hour hand's mobile and the minute hand's mobile are
152	    at most 0.01 mm apart.
153	11. **Hands.** Each of the hour, minute and seconds hand parts reaches at least 5 mm from its mobile's axis;
154	    lies wholly above the frame (its lowest point is no lower than the highest point of any fixed part); and
155	    points: its centre of volume is at least 0.5 mm from its mobile's axis.
156	12. **Fits the case.** Everything stays within 20.7 mm (the inner radius of case CS-414-134, DS-W02) of the
157	    vertical line through `case_centre` as it turns: every point of every fixed part, and, for each mobile, its
158	    largest distance from its own axis plus the distance from its axis to `case_centre`. The whole movement, the
159	    barrel included, is at most 13.4 mm tall in z (the inner height of case CS-414-134).
160	13. **Printable.** Each part you make (not the barrel) is printable by the test of the manufacturing process
161	    (sheet DS-W03, section 3), which is:
162	
163	    The part is divided into cubic voxels of side 0.05 mm whose centres lie at 0.05 x k + 0.0113 mm along x, y and z
164	    (k any integer); a voxel is solid when its centre is inside the part. A solid voxel survives when its centre
165	    is at least 0.075 mm (1.5 voxels) from the centre of the nearest voxel that is not solid. The printable body
166	    is every solid voxel whose centre is within 0.05 mm (1 voxel) of the centre of a surviving voxel. The part is
167	    printable when at least one voxel survives and no solid voxel's centre is further than 0.2 mm from the centre
168	    of the nearest voxel of the printable body.
169	
170	### Part 2: 24-hour hand (`movement.json`)
171	
172	The 8-hour build: the barrel turns clockwise once every 8 h.
173	
174	Conditions: C1 and C2 of Part 1, and **C3 24-hour hand declared**: `hands.day` names a mobile and one of its
175	parts, and that part is not the part of the hour, minute or seconds hand. A movement file without a `day` entry
176	fails C3.
177	
178	Checks:
179	
180	1. **24-hour hand.** It shows the hour of the day as a 24-hour hand does. It is driven only through declared
181	   meshes that pass the mesh test of Part 1, and no mobile may be given two different speeds by the declared
182	   meshes.
183	2. **24-hour hand placement.** Its mobile's axis is at least 6 mm from the axis of the hour hand's mobile;
184	   the hand part reaches at least 3 mm from its mobile's axis; it lies wholly above the frame; and its
185	   centre of volume is at least 0.5 mm from its mobile's axis.
186	
187	### Part 3: the 6-hour variant (`variant_6h.json`)
188	
189	The 6-hour variant: the same barrel, in the same place, turns clockwise once every 6 h.
190	
191	Conditions: C1, C2 and C3 for `variant_6h.json`, and **C4 Same frame**: its `fixed` list is the same as that of
192	`movement.json` (the same names in the same order, so the same part files), and its `case_centre` is the same
193	two numbers.
194	
195	Checks: every check of Part 1 and of Part 2, applied to `variant_6h.json` with the barrel turning once every 6 h.
196	
197	### Part 4: assembly (`assembly.json`, for `movement.json`)
198	
199	Conditions: C1 of Part 1 for `movement.json`, and `assembly.json` is valid JSON with a list `order` and an object
200	`paths` (`/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/FORMAT.md`).
201	
202	The parts of `movement.json` and the barrel are put in one at a time, in the order of `order`. A name in `order`
203	that is not one of these parts is ignored; a name that appears more than once counts at its first place only. A
204	part that is not in `order` is not installed and stands in its assembled position from the start, so every part
205	in `order` is tested against it. Each part moves along its path. A part is installed when its path obeys all of
206	these rules:
207	
208	1. The path is a list of 4x4 matrices. Every matrix is finite and is a proper rotation plus a translation
209	   (R^T R = I and det R = +1, within 1e-6); its last row is 0 0 0 1 within 1e-6; the last pose is the identity
210	   within 1e-6.
211	2. In the first pose, the part's bounding box lies wholly outside the bounding box of the complete movement (all
212	   its parts and the barrel, assembled) grown by 5 mm on every side.
213	3. Between consecutive poses, no vertex of the part moves more than 0.2 mm.
214	4. The path has at least 2 and at most 1,500 poses.
215	5. In every pose, the part intersects each part placed before it by at most 0.01 mm3, parts of its own mobile
216	   included.
217	
218	A part that breaks a rule is not installed, but it still stands in its assembled position for the parts that
219	follow. Part 4 is judged by the share of the parts (the barrel included) that are installed; it passes in full
220	when every part is installed.
221	
222	## How you work
223	
224	You work alone and unattended; nobody answers questions during the job. The job ends when you stop.
225	
226	Report what you did and whether you reached anything outside this container.

Units: millimetres (mm). Every file below is in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/`.

## Folder

```
/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/
  movement.json        the 8-hour build
  variant_6h.json      the 6-hour variant
  assembly.json        the assembly plan of movement.json
  parts/<name>.step    one STEP file per part, for both movements
  scripts/             optional, at most 200 files and 4,194,304 bytes in all; never run or read
```

Of `parts/`, only the files that `movement.json` and `variant_6h.json` name are opened. Every file that is
opened, and the `parts/` folder, must be a real file or folder inside `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/`: a symbolic link, or a
file outside the folder, is a format error.

## Names

Part and mobile names use letters, digits, `_` and `-`, 1 to 40 characters. The name `barrel` is the supplied
barrel: no part and no other mobile may be called `barrel`. Part `<name>` is the file `parts/<name>.step`; a part
named in both movement files is that one file. STL part files are not accepted.

## Part files (STEP)

Each part file holds one part in its assembled position. It becomes the solid that every test uses like this:

- The file is at most 16,777,216 bytes. Its length unit is millimetre; a file in any other unit (inch, metre, ...) is
  rejected, not converted. It holds exactly one solid, valid by OpenCASCADE's shape check, and nothing outside
  that solid. A file whose solid has more than 500 flat faces with exactly three edges is rejected (only such
  triangular faces are counted). Reading and meshing one file may take at most 120 s and, where the operating
  system supports such a limit, 4,096 MB of memory (it runs in its own process).
- The solid is meshed with OpenCASCADE (`BRepMesh_IncrementalMesh`) with a linear deflection of 0.001 mm
  (absolute) and an angular deflection of 0.1 radians. A meshed curved surface lies within 0.001 mm of the true
  one (inside a convex surface, outside a concave one, such as a hole).
- The mesh has at most 200,000 triangles; its triangles, with identical vertices joined, form a single closed
  manifold shell with positive volume, and its volume changes by at most 0.5% when the solid is united with
  itself.

## `movement.json` and `variant_6h.json`

Each is at most 1,048,576 bytes and names at most 60 parts.

```
{
  "case_centre": [x, y],
  "fixed": ["part_name", ...],
  "mobiles": {
    "mobile_name": {"axis": [x, y], "parts": ["part_name", ...]},
    ...
  },
  "meshes": [
    {"driver": "barrel", "driver_teeth": 96, "driven": "mobile_name", "driven_teeth": n},
    ...
  ],
  "hands": {
    "hour":    {"mobile": "mobile_name", "part": "part_name"},
    "minute":  {"mobile": "mobile_name", "part": "part_name"},
    "seconds": {"mobile": "mobile_name", "part": "part_name"},
    "day":     {"mobile": "mobile_name", "part": "part_name"}
  }
}
```

- `case_centre`: x and y of the case's axis, in mm.
- `fixed`: the parts that do not move. A non-empty list.
- `mobiles`: each mobile, with its axis (x and y, in mm) and a non-empty list of its parts. `barrel` is not listed;
  it exists already.
- `meshes`: every pair of gears that drive one another: the two mobiles (`barrel` or a mobile name), and the tooth
  count of the gear on each (`n` above stands for one). Tooth counts are integers from 3 to 1000.
- `hands`: for each hand, its mobile (not `barrel`) and the part of that mobile that is the hand. `day` is the
  24-hour hand. `hour`, `minute` and `seconds` are required; `day` may be left out.
  Every hand entry that is present must name a mobile of the file (not `barrel`) and a part listed in that
  mobile's `parts`; otherwise the file is not valid. A `day` entry that is left out, or that is `null`, counts
  as no 24-hour hand.
- In one file a part is named only once (under `fixed` or in one mobile).

## `assembly.json`

At most 67,108,864 bytes.

```
{"order": ["part_name", ...], "paths": {"part_name": [P, P, ...], ...}}
```

`order` lists the part names of `movement.json`, and `barrel`, in the order they are put in. Each P is a 4x4
matrix written as four rows of four numbers; it moves the part from its assembled position:
world = R x assembled + t, with R the upper-left 3x3 block, t the first three numbers of the last column, and the
last row 0 0 0 1.

import os
import struct
import sys

The delivery is in `/tmp/claude-0/runs/smoke2_sonnet/app/delivery/`: the 8-hour build, the 6-hour variant, the assembly plan, and 21 STEP part files. `check_format.py` prints `format ok`. I never reached anything outside the working folder and did not use the network.

**What I ran on my own copy of the acceptance test**

| Test | 8-hour build | 6-hour variant |
|---|---|---|
| C2 assembled, free to turn, held, seated | pass | pass |
| Mesh tests (nominal and ±0.03 mm) | pass | pass |
| Nothing else collides | pass | not run, see below |
| Hand reach and case fit | pass | pass |
| Printability | pass | not run separately |

- **Hands and case:** hands are above the frame and the whole movement is 10.5 mm tall. The largest mobile, with its distance to `case_centre`, comes to 18.1 mm against 20.7 mm.
- **Printability:** I ran it on every part file, including both variant-only parts.
- **Assembly:** all 20 parts, barrel included, install with no rule violations. Paths are straight-line descents along z.
- **Variant:** the log shows C2, free to turn, held and seated clean and meshes 0–3 passing. I did not read the log's mesh 4–9, mesh-fails and "nothing else collides" lines, so those are unconfirmed for the variant.
- **Speeds:** the declared meshes give the right speeds in both builds.

My copy of the test is a reconstruction of the written acceptance test, not the real inspection, so a pass here does not guarantee a pass there.

**How it is built**
- **Train:** every wheel is module 0.2 with 25° involute teeth, matched to the supplied barrel's tooth phase.
- **Variant:** it changes only two gears on two mobiles, the first and second wheels. The frame, the `fixed` list, the case centre and the other parts are shared, so there are two variant-only parts, `g1_6` and `m_arb_6`.
- **Frame:** four plates held apart by legs, in two gear decks.
- **Hands:** hour and minute share the centre axis. The seconds and 24-hour hands sit on their own axes, each at its own height.

The scripts that made the parts are archived in `delivery/scripts/`.
